title: The Amber Moth
description: A moth with iridescent wings, caught mid-flutter in a drop of resin and kept intact for millennia.
provenance: Said to have been recovered from a glacial moraine by a surveyor in 1887; catalogued by the Cabinet in 1902.

title: Bone Flute of the Glacier
description: A three-holed flute carved from a vulture wing bone, still able to produce a clear, haunting note.
provenance: Found wrapped in birch bark inside a cave shelter; acquired through a field exchange in 1931.

title: Ochre Star Map
description: A painted slab of stone whose dots seem to trace the winter stars above the hunters' horizon.
provenance: Reported by a shepherd in 1954; its pigment was analysed in 1978.

title: Tablet of the Salt Merchant
description: A clay tablet recording a dispute over a shipment of salt, with an apology scrawled in the margin.
provenance: Recovered from a river-delta archive; transferred to the Cabinet with a bequest in 1911.

title: Sundial of the Seven Shadows
description: A stone dial with seven gnomons, each telling a different civic hour in a city that no longer exists.
provenance: Purchased at auction in 1899, provenance traced to a harbour temple.

title: The Antikythera Echo
description: A corroded bronze gear train, a replica fragment hinting at a lost tradition of analogue computing.
provenance: Cast from a wreck-recovered original; gifted by a diving society in 1960.

title: Roman Glass Tear Vial
description: A slender blue-green vial, reputedly used to gather the tears of mourners.
provenance: Excavated from a roadside tomb; entered the collection in 1923.

title: Jade Cicada
description: A palm-sized cicada carved from jade, placed on the tongue of the departed as a promise of rebirth.
provenance: Acquired from a private collector in 1947 with a handwritten label.

title: Astrolabe of al-Fazari
description: A brass astrolabe engraved with the names of stars in two scripts, one added by a later owner.
provenance: Passed through at least four owners before arriving in 1905.

title: Mappa Mundi Fragment
description: A vellum scrap showing sea monsters, a dog-headed people, and a quiet corner marked "here be dragons".
provenance: Salvaged from a binding in a monastery library; conserved in 1966.

title: Bestiary of Impossible Birds
description: An illuminated manuscript of birds that never lived, with notes on their habits and tempers.
provenance: Copied in a scriptorium; later owned by a notable naturalist.

title: Plague Doctor's Beak Reliquary
description: A leather beak stuffed with herbs and a cloth that still smells faintly of juniper and fear.
provenance: Found in a cellar during demolition in 1912.

title: Apothecary of Lost Remedies
description: A travelling chest of 40 labelled phials, many of whose ingredients no one can now identify.
provenance: Inventoried in a merchant's will; found in an attic in 1938.

title: Cabinet of Wax Fruits
description: A drawer of lifelike wax fruit made to be admired, studied, and (embarrassingly) bitten by the unwary.
provenance: Part of a princely collection dispersed in the seventeenth century.

title: Galileo's Lost Lens
description: A small, slightly cloudy lens ground for a telescope, with a thumbprint pressed into the glass mount.
provenance: Attributed by letter to a workshop in Padua; arrived in 1920.

title: Orrery of the Small Moons
description: A brass planetary model whose clockwork includes moons not discovered for another century.
provenance: Built by an instrument maker for a country gentleman.

title: Clockwork Sparrow
description: A tiny automaton that sings, flaps and cocks its head — then falls silent mid-song.
provenance: Recorded in an inventory of a Swiss maker; arrived in 1928.

title: Difference Engine Gear
description: A single precision gear from a mechanical calculator that was never completed in its maker's lifetime.
provenance: Salvaged from a workshop clear-out; given by a descendant in 1950.

title: Pneumatic Letter Capsule
description: A felt-lined cylinder that once whooshed messages through tubes under the city at tremendous speed.
provenance: Retrieved from a decommissioned exchange in 1969.

title: Magic Lantern of Dr. Vale
description: A lantern with hand-painted glass slides, used in lectures to summon ghosts, comets and sea serpents.
provenance: Owned by an itinerant lecturer; auctioned in 1974.

title: Unknown Phonograph Cylinder
description: A wax cylinder labelled only "Do not play on Sundays". Its contents remain contested.
provenance: Found in a piano bench, accessioned in 1981.

title: The Taxidermy Mermaid
description: A sewn marvel of monkey and fish, once exhibited as a sea-maiden and now celebrated as a masterpiece of hoax.
provenance: Displayed in a travelling show; bought by the Cabinet in 1935.

title: Theremin Prototype
description: An early touchless instrument played by waving the hands in the air; its antennae hum quietly.
provenance: Built in a Moscow lab; arrived via a collector in 1967.

title: Vacuum Tube Radio
description: A walnut-cased radio whose tubes glow amber, tuned to stations that no longer broadcast.
provenance: Donated from a family kitchen in 1990.

title: Cloud Chamber
description: A glass chamber where invisible particles leave brief white trails through vapour.
provenance: Built in a university lab; gifted in 1972.

title: Geiger Counter Prototype
description: A handmade counter that clicks as it senses what the eye cannot.
provenance: Lab-made device acquired in 1958.

title: Sputnik Pocket Model
description: A polished steel sphere with four antennae, sold as a souvenir the year a beeping moon crossed the sky.
provenance: Acquired from a stall in 1958.

title: Golden Record Copy
description: A replica of a record of greetings, songs and sounds sent into the dark for anyone who might listen.
provenance: Produced for an exhibition and added in 1999.

title: Lost Floppy Archive
description: A shoebox of floppy disks, labelled in felt tip, that hold stories nobody can open now.
provenance: Donated anonymously in 2011.

title: Whale Ear-Bone Bell
description: A dense, ringing ear bone from a whale, strung on sinew and used as a bell by coastal hunters.
provenance: Washed from an eroding shore bank; donated by a beachcomber in 1963.
